LISTING OF CLAIMS
This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:
1. (Currently amended) An apparatus for generating a quality diagnostic of analog ECG (electrocardiogram) data, wherein the apparatus comprises: at least a processor; and a memory communicatively connected to the at least a processor, wherein the memory contains instructions configuring the at least a processor to: receive an image of ECG data; extract a plurality of ECG parameters from the image of ECG data; convert the image of the ECG data to one or more digitized ECG signals; validate the one or more digitized ECG signals, wherein validating comprises: classifying the one or more digitized ECG signals to a plurality of preliminary ECG parameters; and determining an accuracy status of the extracted plurality of ECG parameters by comparing the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters to the extracted plurality of ECG parameters, wherein: the accuracy status further comprises a variable indicating accuracy of the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters; determining an accuracy status comprises using a scoring algorithm using a threshold to determine the accuracy status, wherein the accuracy status comprises one of a pass status and a fail status, and wherein the apparatus is configured to generate the threshold by: training a threshold classifier with training data correlating a plurality of annotations indicating abnormalities to a plurality of thresholds; inputting the analog ECG data into the threshold classifier; and outputting, by the threshold classifier, the threshold; and generate a quality diagnostic of the image of ECG data based on validation of the one or more digitized ECG signals, wherein the quality diagnostic represents a degree of quality of the image of ECG data.
2. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the ECG data comprises an ECG printout comprising one or more ECG signals and the plurality of ECG parameters.
3. (Currently amended) The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a machine vision system, wherein the memory contains instructions further configuring the at least a processor to: capture the [[an ]]image of the ECG data; and extract the plurality of ECG parameters from the image.
4. (Original) The apparatus of claim 3, wherein: the machine vision system comprises an optical character recognition reader; and the memory contains instructions further configuring the at least a processor to extract the plurality of ECG parameters from the image using the optical character recognition reader.
5. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein classifying the plurality of digitized ECG signals comprises: training a validation classifier using training data comprising a plurality of digitized ECG signals correlated to a plurality of textbook validators of ECG parameters; inputting the plurality of digitized ECG signals into the validation classifier; and outputting, by the validation classifier, the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters.
6. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein determining an accuracy status comprises using a scoring algorithm using a threshold to determine the accuracy status, wherein the accuracy status comprises one of a pass status and a fail status.
7. (Original) The apparatus of claim 6, wherein the memory contains instructions further configuring the at least a processor to determine the threshold by: training a threshold classifier with training data correlating a plurality of annotations indicating abnormalities to a plurality of thresholds; inputting the analog ECG data into the threshold classifier; and outputting, by the threshold classifier, the threshold.
8. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the quality diagnostic comprises an auditory representation comprising sounds to indicate a pass status or a fail status regarding an overall quality of the analog ECG data.
9. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein generating the quality diagnostic comprises generating a visual representation regarding the quality status of the analog ECG data by: training a diagnostic classifier with training data correlating analog ECG data to a plurality of flags; inputting the analog ECG data into the diagnostic classifier; and outputting, by the diagnostic classifier, one or more flags indicating an issue with the analog ECG data.
10. (Original) The apparatus of claim 1, wherein validating the digitized ECG signals comprises receiving ECG verification data from a user comprising a threshold for a scoring algorithm.
11. (Currently amended) A method for generating a quality diagnostic of analog ECG (electrocardiogram) data, wherein the method comprises: receiving, by at least a processor, an image of ECG data; extracting, by the at least a processor, a plurality of ECG parameters from the image of ECG data; converting, by the at least a processor, the image of ECG data to one or more digitized ECG signals; validating, by the at least a processor, the digitized ECG signals, wherein validating comprises: classifying, by the at least a processor, the plurality of digitized ECG signals to a plurality of preliminary ECG parameters; and determining, by the at least a processor, an accuracy status of the extracted plurality of ECG parameters by comparing the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters to the extracted plurality of ECG parameters, wherein: the accuracy status further comprises a variable indicating accuracy of the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters; determining an accuracy status comprises using a scoring algorithm using a threshold to determine the accuracy status, wherein the accuracy status comprises one of a pass status and a fail status, and wherein generating the threshold further comprises:
training a threshold classifier with training data correlating a plurality of annotations indicating abnormalities to a plurality of thresholds; inputting the analog ECG data into the threshold classifier; and outputting, by the threshold classifier, the threshold; and generating, by the at least a processor, a quality diagnostic of the image of ECG data based on validation of the digitized ECG signals, wherein the quality diagnostic represents a degree of quality of the image of ECG data.
12. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein the ECG data comprises an ECG printout comprising one or more ECG signals and the plurality of ECG parameters.
13. (Currently amended) The method of claim 11, wherein receiving the ECG data comprises: capturing, using a machine vision vision system, the [[an ]]image of the ECG data; and extracting, using the machine vision system, the plurality of ECG parameters from the image.
14. (Original) The method of claim 13, wherein extracting, using the machine vision system, the plurality of ECG parameters further comprises using an using an optical character recognition reader.
15. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein classifying the plurality of digitized ECG signals comprises: training a validation classifier using training data comprising a plurality of digitized ECG signals correlated to a plurality of textbook validators of ECG parameters; inputting the plurality of digitized ECG signals into the validation classifier; and outputting, by the validation classifier, the plurality of preliminary ECG parameters.
16. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein determining an accuracy status comprises using a scoring algorithm using a threshold to determine the accuracy status, wherein the accuracy status comprises one of a pass status and a fail status.
17. (Original) The method of claim 16, wherein using the scoring algorithm comprises determining the threshold by: training a threshold classifier with training data correlating a plurality of annotations indicating abnormalities to a plurality of thresholds; inputting the analog ECG data into the threshold classifier; and outputting, by the threshold classifier, the threshold.
18. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein the quality diagnostic comprises an auditory representation comprising sounds to indicate a pass status or a fail status regarding an overall quality of the analog ECG data.
19. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein generating the quality diagnostic comprises generating a visual representation regarding the quality status of the analog ECG data by: training a diagnostic classifier with training data correlating analog ECG data to a plurality of flags; inputting the analog ECG data into the diagnostic classifier; and outputting, by the diagnostic classifier, one or more flags indicating an issue with the analog ECG data.
20. (Original) The method of claim 11, wherein validating the digitized ECG signals comprises receiving ECG verification data from user comprising a threshold for a scoring algorithm.
